answer: Spectral entry auction. Each identity must win a unique random slot in a shared frequency band at registration; slots are re-drawn periodically along a velvet curve that shifts the cost surface unpredictably. Because each new clone needs its own winning bid, marginal identities pay rising prices while the attacker's original slot keeps its value fixed. The auction acts as a prism, splitting a bulk registration into many independent, costly contests. A vertex cap limits slots per operator cluster, so a clone's expected gain falls below its bid plus re-draw cost.
